metaTitle: Contractor Invoice Template: Free Trades & Labor Bills
metaDescription: Download our free contractor invoice template for construction and trade pros. Itemize materials, labor hours, and milestone payments with no watermarks.
intro: A contractor invoice template is a standardized billing statement used by independent contractors, trade specialists, and 1099 workers to bill for labor and materials. It specifies milestones or hourly rates, itemizes supply costs, calculates sales tax, and outlines agreed payment terms for commercial compliance.

howTo.title: How to Fill a Contractor Billing Template
howTo.subtitle: Clear, dispute-proof contractor invoices in three simple steps.

steps.title: Enter Contractor and Jobsite Details
steps.description: Add your trade business name, state licence number, client billing address, and the physical jobsite address where work took place.
steps.tip: Always record the jobsite address separately from the client's office address.

steps.title: Itemize Labor, Supplies, and Permits
steps.description: Separate skilled labor hours from materials, building fixtures, and permit fees for complete billing transparency.
steps.tip: Include the client's work order or purchase order (PO) number to avoid billing delays.

steps.title: Download the PDF or Print on the Jobsite
steps.description: Generate an instant vector PDF to email from your phone or print a hard copy directly for on-site sign-off.
steps.tip: State payment milestones clearly (e.g., 50% deposit). When deposit funds are paid, issue an itemized receipt using our Online Receipt Maker with Items.

faq.title: Contractor Invoice Template FAQs
faq.subtitle: Answers to common questions about trade billing, materials tax, and milestone payments.

items.question: What must a contractor invoice include to prevent client payment disputes?
items.answer: A contractor invoice must include your business name, license number, client details, jobsite location, unique invoice number, dates worked, itemized labor hours, materials costs, and payment terms. Explicitly separating labor from materials clarifies sales tax obligations and protects your statutory mechanics lien rights across commercial and residential projects.

items.question: Why should contractors separate labor and materials on billing templates?
items.answer: Separating labor and materials clarifies project billing and simplifies statutory sales tax reporting across jurisdictions. In most regions, sales tax applies strictly to physical construction materials while skilled contractor labor is exempt. Clear line-item breakdowns prevent client disputes, make job costing transparent, and streamline annual trade tax filings.

items.question: Are invoices created with this contractor bill format legally valid?
items.answer: Yes, contractor bills created with this format are legally valid commercial documents for trade accounting and contracts. When paired with signed work authorizations, material receipts, and approved change orders, these invoices provide complete, dispute-proof legal evidence for commercial clients, general contractor billing, and statutory tax compliance audits.

items.question: Can contractors add a company logo and license badge?
items.answer: Yes, you can upload your trade company logo, guild badge, or state licensing credential directly to the invoice letterhead. Displaying your branding and credentials prominently reinforces professional authority. It also helps commercial property managers and general contractors verify your trade legitimacy before approving disbursements.

items.question: What is the difference between a contractor invoice and a receipt?
items.answer: A contractor invoice requests payment for completed labor and jobsite supplies before settlement occurs, whereas a receipt acknowledges payment after funds clear. Issue an itemized invoice upon hitting project milestones to request draws. Once your client pays by transfer or cheque, issue an official receipt to acknowledge settled accounts.
